sentences.text: Im November wird es in Deutschland kalt.
sentences.translation: In November it gets cold in Germany.
sentences.grammarNote: 'es wird kalt' = it gets cold: impersonal 'es' + 'werden' + adjective. 'im' = 'in dem', used with months.

sentences.text: Am Morgen ist es oft neblig und grau.
sentences.translation: In the morning it is often foggy and grey.
sentences.grammarNote: Time phrase first, so the verb 'ist' comes second and 'es' moves after it. 'am' = 'an dem' (Dativ).

sentences.text: Die Tage werden kürzer.
sentences.translation: The days are getting shorter.
sentences.grammarNote: Comparative = adjective + '-er'; short adjectives often add an Umlaut: kurz → kürzer.

sentences.text: In den Bergen fällt schon der erste Schnee.
sentences.translation: The first snow is already falling in the mountains.
sentences.grammarNote: Verb-second rule: the place phrase comes first, so the subject 'der erste Schnee' goes after the verb.

words.grammar: fallen · Präsens · 3. Person Singular · a → ä

sentences.text: Viele Menschen trinken jetzt gern einen heißen Tee.
sentences.translation: Many people now like to drink a hot tea.
sentences.grammarNote: 'gern' + verb = to like doing something. 'einen heißen Tee' is masculine Akkusativ: einen + -en.

words.grammar: gern · verb + gern = etwas gern tun

sentences.text: Am 11. November feiern viele Kinder Sankt Martin.
sentences.translation: On November 11, many children celebrate St. Martin's Day.
sentences.grammarNote: Dates use 'am' + ordinal number: 'am elften November'. The verb 'feiern' stays in second position.

sentences.text: Sie laufen am Abend mit bunten Laternen durch die Straßen.
sentences.translation: In the evening they walk through the streets with colorful lanterns.
sentences.grammarNote: 'mit' always takes Dativ (mit bunten Laternen); 'durch' always takes Akkusativ (durch die Straßen).

sentences.text: Die Kinder singen zusammen Lieder.
sentences.translation: The children sing songs together.
sentences.grammarNote: Many neuter nouns form the plural with '-er': das Lied → die Lieder.

sentences.text: Sankt Martin hat seinen Mantel mit einem armen Mann geteilt.
sentences.translation: St. Martin shared his coat with a poor man.
sentences.grammarNote: Perfekt: 'hat' + past participle 'geteilt' at the end. 'seinen Mantel' is masculine Akkusativ.

sentences.text: Danach essen viele Familien eine Martinsgans.
sentences.translation: Afterwards many families eat a St. Martin's goose.
sentences.grammarNote: Compound noun: Martin + s + Gans. The last part decides the gender: die Gans → die Martinsgans.

words.grammar: die Martinsgans · Akkusativ · compound: Martin + Gans (goose)

sentences.text: Ende November öffnen in Deutschland die Weihnachtsmärkte.
sentences.translation: At the end of November the Christmas markets open in Germany.
sentences.grammarNote: Time phrase 'Ende November' (no preposition needed) comes first, so the subject comes after the verb.

words.grammar: der Weihnachtsmarkt · Nominativ · Plural · Weihnachten + Markt

sentences.text: Es gibt kleine Häuser aus Holz mit vielen Lichtern.
sentences.translation: There are small wooden huts with lots of lights.
sentences.grammarNote: 'es gibt' + Akkusativ = there is/are. 'aus Holz' = made of wood ('aus' + Dativ).

words.grammar: das Licht · Dativ · Plural · -n in Dativ Plural

sentences.text: Die Leute trinken Glühwein und essen Lebkuchen.
sentences.translation: People drink mulled wine and eat gingerbread.
sentences.grammarNote: No article for things in general: 'Glühwein trinken' = drink (some) mulled wine.

sentences.text: Der Markt in Nürnberg ist sehr bekannt.
sentences.translation: The market in Nuremberg is very famous.
sentences.grammarNote: 'sein' + adjective: the adjective after 'ist' takes no ending.

sentences.text: Viele Menschen kaufen hier ihre ersten Geschenke.
sentences.translation: Many people buy their first presents here.
sentences.grammarNote: 'ihre' = their (plural possessive). 'ersten' has a weak ending after the possessive in the plural.

sentences.text: Im Herbst und im Winter sind viele Menschen erkältet.
sentences.translation: In autumn and winter many people have a cold.
sentences.grammarNote: 'erkältet sein' = to have a cold. The participle of 'sich erkälten' is used like an adjective.

words.grammar: sich erkälten → erkältet · Partizip II als Adjektiv

sentences.text: Sie haben Schnupfen, Husten oder Halsschmerzen.
sentences.translation: They have a runny nose, a cough or a sore throat.
sentences.grammarNote: Illnesses with 'haben' often need no article. 'Halsschmerzen' is almost always plural.

sentences.text: Ärzte sagen: „Waschen Sie sich oft die Hände!“
sentences.translation: Doctors say: "Wash your hands often!"
sentences.grammarNote: Polite imperative: verb first + 'Sie'. Body parts use 'sich' + definite article, not 'Ihre'.

sentences.text: Wer krank ist, soll zu Hause bleiben.
sentences.translation: Anyone who is sick should stay at home.
sentences.grammarNote: 'wer' = whoever; in the 'wer' clause the verb goes to the end. Modal 'soll' + infinitive 'bleiben' at the end.

sentences.text: Viel Schlaf und warmer Tee helfen auch.
sentences.translation: Lots of sleep and warm tea also help.
sentences.grammarNote: No article → the adjective shows the case: 'warmer Tee' = masculine Nominativ, strong ending '-er'.
